title: A generic fibre basis becomes universally injective on a base open
statement: Let $R\to B$ be a flat homomorphism of commutative rings of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map, def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Suppose that every fibre $B\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak s)$, for a prime $\mathfrak s\subset R$, is geometrically integral: after every field extension of $\kappa(\mathfrak s)$ it is a nonzero integral domain [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible, def-pc-integral-scheme]. Let $M$ be a finitely presented $B$-module [def-sc-finitely-presented-module] which is flat as an $R$-module. Let $\mathfrak r\subset R$ be prime and put $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak rB$; assume explicitly that $\mathfrak p$ is prime and contracts to $\mathfrak r$. Let $a\geq0$ and let $\alpha:B^{\oplus a}\to M$ be $B$-linear such that $\alpha\otimes_B\kappa(\mathfrak p):\kappa(\mathfrak p)^{\oplus a}\to M\otimes_B\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is an isomorphism. Then there is $f\in R\setminus\mathfrak r$ such that $\alpha_f:B_f^{\oplus a}\to M_f$ is universally injective over $R_f$: for every $R_f$-module $L$, the map $L\otimes_{R_f}B_f^{\oplus a}\to L\otimes_{R_f}M_f$ induced by $\alpha_f$ is injective. Here $B_f$ and $M_f$ mean localization at the powers of the image of $f$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]; residue fields and tensor products are [def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-affine-flat-module-localization-preserves-flatness] to the given $R\to B$, the $R$-flat $B$-module $M$, and the multiplicative subset $B\setminus\mathfrak p$. It gives that $M_{\mathfrak p}$ is flat over $R$. Every $s\in R\setminus\mathfrak r$ maps outside $\mathfrak p$, since $\mathfrak p\cap R=\mathfrak r$, and hence acts invertibly on $M_{\mathfrak p}$. Thus $M_{\mathfrak p}$ is an $R_{\mathfrak r}$-module by $(u/s)(x/t)=ux/(st)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-localization] with $A=R$, $W=R\setminus\mathfrak r$, $A\prime=R_{\mathfrak r}$, and module $M_{\mathfrak p}$ to conclude that $M_{\mathfrak p}$ is flat over $R_{\mathfrak r}$.

Apply [lem-sfb-local-flat-generic-basis-universal-injectivity], renaming its base prime $\mathfrak p$ as our $\mathfrak r$, its algebra prime $\mathfrak q$ as our $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak rB$, its module $E$ as $M$, and its rank $r$ as $a$. The flat finite presentation of $B/R$, geometric integrality of every fibre, primeness and contraction of $\mathfrak p$, finite presentation of $M/B$, and residue-field isomorphism for the specified $\alpha$ are exactly the hypotheses of this item. Step 1 supplies its remaining hypothesis, flatness of $M_{\mathfrak p}$ over $R_{\mathfrak r}$. The cited statement therefore provides $f\in R\setminus\mathfrak r$ such that $L\otimes_{R_f}\alpha_f$ is injective for every $R_f$-module $L$. Its localizations use the image of this same $f$ in $B$, so these are precisely $B_f$, $M_f$, and the induced map in the conclusion.
